_comment: AcouDiet frozen feature spec -- SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for both training and app side.
_comment_2: Any change here MUST be mirrored via the change-propagate list in SPEC-C-03 section 7 (14 items).
_comment_3: All values are FROZEN as of 2026-09-10, REVISED 2026-09-12 by ADR-21 (Mel front-end v1.1) after the delivered model proved the training-side chain differed. See _decisions for the recorded choices and their rationale.
_comment_4: ADR-21 note: preemphasis_boundary / power_to_db_ref / normalization / n_frames / input_shape were REVISED in place. The superseded values live in _decisions.mel_frontend_v1_1.supersedes, not deleted, so the change stays auditable.

n_frames.reason: ADR-P1 froze 129 raw STFT frames and put all 129 into the tensor. The delivered model's input tensor is [1,128,128,1] -- physically 128 frames -- so 129 can never be fed to it. The raw STFT frame count is still 129 (now recorded as raw_mel_frames); what changed is that the tail frame is DROPPED before normalisation, exactly as the training-side pipeline does.
n_frames.rationale: librosa center=True yields n_samples // hop + 1 = 65536 // 512 + 1 = 129 frames for a 4.096 s window. Option B adopted: keep the 4.096 s window (exactly 2^16 samples at 16 kHz, covering about 4-8 chewing cycles) and accept a 129-frame input. The non-power-of-two frame count is inconsequential for a GlobalAveragePooling classifier, and 4.096 s is already frozen in every downstream document.

rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: Would require re-deriving patch_seconds / patch_samples / input_shape across every document and every test fixture, for no modelling benefit.

mel_numerics.issue: Four Mel/STFT parameters were named as risk points by SPEC-P-04 section 10 but had no frozen value. Each one changes the numbers the Kotlin front-end produces, so any mismatch silently breaks the atol=1e-3 cross-language parity gate (PLAN-T-08).
mel_numerics.superseded_reason: pad_mode / mel_htk / mel_norm are UNCHANGED and still correct. Only power_to_db_ref changed: 1.0 -> "patch_max", because the delivered model was trained with a patch-relative dB scale. See _decisions.mel_frontend_v1_1.
mel_numerics.rationale: All four are librosa's own defaults, stated explicitly so the Kotlin implementation has an unambiguous target: center=True pads with zeros (pad_mode='constant'); power_to_db uses ref=1.0 so that the fixed dB clip of FF-08 is applied to an absolute scale (ref=np.max would make the clip patch-relative and re-introduce the domain-shift trap); the mel filterbank uses the Slaney scale and Slaney area normalisation (htk=False, norm='slaney') rather than HTK.

rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: reflect padding changes the first frames; ref=np.max makes the dB range patch-relative (domain shift at inference); htk=True changes filter shapes. All three would need the Python side changed too and would still be harder to reproduce in Kotlin.

preprocess_scope.issue: SPEC-P-03 section 4 listed a high-pass filter whose cutoff and order were never frozen, and section 10 left the pre-emphasis first-sample convention undecided. An unfrozen filter on the Kotlin side cannot pass the parity gate against a Python side that does not run it.
preprocess_scope.superseded_reason: highpass stays removed and loudness_normalization stays training_only. Only preemphasis_boundary changed: first_sample_passthrough -> continuous stream previous raw sample. See _decisions.mel_frontend_v1_1.
preprocess_scope.rationale: The master plan section 3.7 already says spectral subtraction is dropped and only pre-emphasis plus loudness normalisation are kept -- a high-pass was never in the frozen plan. Removing it also removes an unfrozen parameter that could only break parity. Pre-emphasis leaves the first sample unchanged (x[-1] = x[0]), matching librosa's lfilter initial condition. Loudness normalisation (LUFS) is a TRAINING-TIME augmentation only (target -23 LUFS, see T-03): at inference the FF-08 fixed dB clip plus per-patch min-max already makes the model input scale-invariant, so running LUFS on-device would add cost for no benefit.

rejected_alternative.highpass: 2nd-order Butterworth at 20 Hz on both sides
rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: fmin=20 already discards everything below 20 Hz in the mel filterbank, and pre-emphasis already suppresses low frequencies; adding a filter that must be bit-matched in two languages is pure risk.

vad_parameters.issue: PLAN-P-02's Kotlin skeleton consumed four VAD parameters (noiseFloorInit / noiseFloorMin / marginDbToLinear / alpha) that did not exist anywhere in this file. The end-point detector therefore had unfrozen thresholds -- the same defect class as ADR-16/17, found by auditing references against the SSOT.
vad_parameters.rationale: The detector is a per-frame energy comparison against an ADAPTIVE noise floor, so its four constants live under behavior next to envelope_frame_ms / envelope_hop_ms / envelope_length (the same framing pass produces both the VAD decision and the 819-point RMS envelope). Values are linear RMS except the margin: noise_floor_init = 0.001 (-60 dBFS) is a typical quiet-room floor; noise_floor_min = 0.0003 (-70 dBFS) stops the floor from collapsing on digital silence; voiced_margin_db = 6 dB above the floor is the standard hysteresis-free margin for this kind of detector; noise_floor_alpha = 0.95 is a slow one-pole update (time constant about 20 frames at the 32 ms hop, i.e. about 0.64 s) so a single chew transient cannot drag the floor up. A frame counts as voiced when rms > noise_floor * 10^(voiced_margin_db / 20).

rejected_alternative.scheme: fixed absolute threshold instead of an adaptive floor
rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: Phone microphone gain varies far too much between devices for an absolute RMS threshold to transfer; adaptation is what makes the same constants work across handsets.

class_table.issue: The training side delivered a corpus whose six classes are chips / cabbage / gummies / noodles / carrot / drink, replacing apple (id 1), cookie (id 2) and bread (id 3). One of the replacements, noodles, was FF-19's explicitly reserved class ('不进 v1.0'), and the project carried four structural guards against it: the artifact gate's CUT_TOKENS, the ablation FORBIDDEN list, foods.schema.json's additionalProperties:false refusal, and SPEC-U-03's ban on the Chinese word 面条.
class_table.rationale: FF-19 is amended by explicit user decision (option A of the 2026-09-12 review) rather than worked around. Three points were settled at the same time: (1) noodles leaves the reserve list because the training corpus actually contains it; nuts stays reserved, so the guard mechanism itself is kept, only its membership changed. (2) structure.healthy_labels becomes [cabbage, carrot, noodles] -- the ID set is unchanged at {1,3,4}, so every scoring fixture keeps its meaning while the names follow the new table. (3) chips' attribute changes to 脆性高加工零食 and gummies' is 黏弹性零食, so the attribute can no longer be derived from a hardcoded classId switch: it is snapshotted from foods.json, which is what API-03 section 2 required all along.

rejected_alternative.option: keep FF-19 frozen and map the trainer's folders onto the old class names (Noodles->bread, Gummies->cookie, Cabbage->apple)
rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: The corpus genuinely is cabbage, gummies and noodles; presenting a bowl of noodles to the user as 面包 would be a false statement in the UI, and cabbage (脆爽蔬菜) is not the same food category as apple (脆爽果蔬). Renaming the classes is honest; renaming the data is not.

class_table.known_data_risk: noodles (412) and drink (293) are below SPEC-T-01's 500-fragments-per-class floor, and cabbage is exactly at it. The T-01 --strict gate would exit 3 on this corpus; the FF-19 four-class downgrade switch should be evaluated before any accuracy claim.

mel_frontend_v1_1.issue: The model group delivered mobile_release/v1 (fp32 + int8 dynamic-range + int8 full-integer). Its feature_config.json describes a Mel front-end that is NOT the one this repository froze: patch_max dB instead of ref=1.0, per-patch minmax instead of a fixed [-80,0] dB clip, the tail STFT frame dropped to give 128 frames, and pre-emphasis carried across patches from the previous RAW sample. Two of those differences are directly visible in the artifact: the delivered input tensor is [1,128,128,1] (so 129 frames cannot even be written to it), and the first three ops of the graph are MUL(x2) -> ADD(-1) -> CONCATENATION(input,input,input), i.e. the release note's rescaling + three-channel module exists in the shipped file.
mel_frontend_v1_1.why_this_is_not_optional: This is a training/inference skew, not a preference. The parity gate (PLAN-T-08) proves the Kotlin and Python implementations agree with EACH OTHER; it cannot see the training side. With both sides consistently implementing the old chain the gate passed while the shipped model was fed a tensor from a different distribution -- exactly the failure the gate was built to prevent, one level up. Aligning the front end to the delivered spec is the only way the shipped model can work at all.
mel_frontend_v1_1.rationale: Three points settle it. (1) The tensor shape decides n_frames: 128, with the raw STFT frame count 129 preserved as raw_mel_frames so the two numbers can never be confused again. Frame selection is applied BEFORE per-patch minmax (the released operation_order is mel -> power_to_db -> drop_tail -> minmax), so the dB reference is the max over the full 129 frames while the min-max window is the kept 128 -- reproducing that order matters, and the Kotlin code follows it literally rather than re-deriving it. (2) power_to_db_ref becomes the string "patch_max": ADR-16 rejected ref=np.max as a domain-shift trap, and that rejection was sound FOR THE CHAIN IT WAS FROZEN FOR; it does not apply now, because the delivered model was trained with a patch-relative scale and an inference chain that disagrees with training is the larger error. (3) DC removal is REMOVED: the delivered operation_order has no DC stage, so keeping ours would inject an unmodelled transform between the microphone and the model.

rejected_alternative.option: keep the frozen v1.0 chain and ask the model group to retrain against it
rejected_alternative.reason_rejected: The model exists and is trained; the frozen chain is documentation. Shipping the model as delivered costs one front-end change that is fully verified by an existing cross-language gate; retraining costs a full training cycle plus a new export plus a new parity run, and the accuracy numbers in the release note would not carry over.

honest_limits: The accuracy figures (fp32 55.7%, int8 52.5% on the public test set) come from the model group and CANNOT be re-measured here: ai/data/splits, ai/data/raw and ai/data/augmented are empty in this repository, so there is no labelled corpus to evaluate against.

What WAS measured locally: with the v1.1 chain the delivered fp32 model runs over the repository's own 20 s demo wav and returns a single stable label (carrot) on all 32 patches with mean top-1 confidence 0.839; the v1.0 chain cannot produce a tensor the model accepts at all (shape [1,128,129,1] vs [1,128,128,1]).

Top-1 confidence is NOT accuracy. The int8 artifact showed a HIGHER mean confidence (0.883) on the same input while the release note reports it as 3.25 pp LESS accurate -- a good reminder that confidence is not evidence of correctness.
mel_frontend_v1_1.boundary_impact: Top-level SSOT keys: db_clip_range (a List of 2) is REMOVED and replaced by normalization_epsilon / normalization_output_min / normalization_output_max; raw_mel_frames, power_to_db_amin, frame_selection, operation_order and model_internal_preprocessing are ADDED. The generated Dart/Kotlin constants and app/assets/feature_config.json are regenerated from this file; the start-up handshake grows from 12 to 15 compared fields so the newly load-bearing numerics (rawMelFrames, preemphasisBoundary, powerToDbRef, topDb, normalization) are covered.

supersedes.FF-11_n_frames: 129 raw frames fed to the tensor (ADR-P1)

mel_frontend_v1_1.closes_open_item: ADR-20 recorded one unresolved item: the model group's report said the Kotlin side feeds float32[1,128,128,1], which disagreed with the frozen n_frames=129, and asked whether that was a typo or the real shape. The delivered artifact answers it: the shape is real. ADR-20's third 'correction' (that the 1->3 channel expansion is a 1x1 Conv2D named channel_expand rather than Rescaling + Concatenate) describes THIS REPOSITORY's placeholder ai/src/model.py, not the delivered model -- the shipped graph really is MUL(2) -> ADD(-1) -> CONCATENATE(input,input,input).

agent._comment_2: Nothing here participates in the 15-field start-up handshake (API-00 section 3.6). These values do not change any tensor semantic, and check_bridge_symmetry.py asserts the handshake field set is exactly those 15.
